question: Which Go MCP SDKs apply to the server side?
evidence: Same SDK landscape as the client mission — mark3labs/mcp-go primary; an official MCP org Go SDK has been incubated. Server-side bring-up patterns are similar.
decision_or_followup: Hand-roll the server too; reuse JSON-RPC framing from the client mission.

question: Is JSON-RPC framing reusable across client + server?
evidence: Yes — JSON-RPC 2.0 framing is symmetric. Only the directionality of who-issues-which method differs.
decision_or_followup: Reuse core/mcp/client/jsonrpc/ in this mission OR refactor to core/mcp/jsonrpc/ during this mission's WP02.

question: Is stdlib net/http sufficient for streamable-HTTP server?
evidence: Yes — http.Server with one handler at / suffices. Content-type discrimination on response (application/json vs text/event-stream) covers single + streaming responses.
decision_or_followup: Use stdlib net/http; no third-party HTTP library.

question: How does stdio mode prevent stdout corruption?
evidence: Internal logging MUST route to stderr or the event log; the harness MUST refuse to start in stdio mode if stdout is unsuitable (TTY with colorization, buffered). The MCP spec allocates stderr as out-of-band.
decision_or_followup: Add startup gate; route all logging away from stdout.

question: How is server-side cancellation propagated?
evidence: Client sends notifications/cancelled with the request id; server cancels the corresponding handler context.
decision_or_followup: Per-handler context.WithCancel; the dispatch table tracks cancel funcs by request id.

question: How is sampling routed server-side?
evidence: Two models: (a) server uses its own LLM for sampling, (b) server requests sampling/createMessage from the client and the client owns the LLM. The MCP spec describes (b) as the canonical pattern.
decision_or_followup: Plan resolves toward (a) — internal LLM under bundle profile — to match spec FR-009 and OQ-3 default. Tools that prefer (b) can issue regular sampling requests over the session.

question: How does graceful shutdown work?
evidence: http.Server.Shutdown stops accepting new connections and waits for in-flight handlers; configurable drain timeout; force-close after.
decision_or_followup: Wire into core.Core.Shutdown; default drain 30 s.

question: Origin/CORS controls?
evidence: http.Request.Header.Get(Origin) checked against configurable allowlist; rejected requests get HTTP 403 and an audit event.
decision_or_followup: Implement in middleware; default allowlist localhost-only.

question: Bearer-token auth?
evidence: Authorization: Bearer <token> header; server resolves expected token via core/secrets at start; constant-time compare on each request.
decision_or_followup: Required when bound to non-loopback; optional otherwise.

question: How are bundle-published prompts/resources sourced?
evidence: Active bundle resolver exposes Prompts() and Resources() per resolved bundle; server queries at request time (no caching since bundles may reload).
decision_or_followup: Server holds a bundle.Resolver reference; queries on each list/read.

question: Is replay determinism different for inbound MCP?
evidence: Yes — tools have side effects (run_bundle mutates). Replay records inbound entries as observations; does NOT re-execute tools.
decision_or_followup: Audit emits sufficient context for replay reconstruction; no auto-replay-execution layer.

question: Are there known credential leak shapes in tool results?
evidence: Same patterns as MCP-client mission. Tool implementations should not return credential bytes; defense-in-depth redaction in the event-log pipeline.

question: Day-one tool catalog scope?
evidence: FR-018 specifies five harness-native tools: run_bundle, list_bundles, query_event_log, list_sessions, list_provider_profiles. Mix of read-only and one mutator.
decision_or_followup: Ship the five; trim during WP planning if any turns out to be operationally unsafe to expose by default.
